items.title: How to start eating plant-based, without missing out on nutrients or foods you enjoy
items.standfirst: Experts agree that if you’re thinking of changing your diet, start small and keep your goals in mindAt this point, the environmental effects of the meat industry have been well-established: one 2021 study found that meat accounts for nearly 60% of all greenhouse gases from food production, and a 2025 report estimated that animal agriculture was responsible for 12%-19% of total human-caused greenhouse gases.According to the United Nations, one of the best things people can do to reduce their personal carbon footprint is shift from a diet heavy in meat to one that is more plant-based. Many of us know this, but in the US and UK, fewer than 5% of adults identify as vegetarian or vegan. One of the biggest obstacles, according to experts? People think it’s too hard. Continue reading...

items.title: Trump takes 500 actions to weaken cancer protections, new report says
items.standfirst: Natural Resources Defense Council shows how federal rules changes will increase public’s exposure to carcinogensAmid a rise in early onset cancer, the Trump administration has taken more than 500 actions to systematically dismantle protections against carcinogens once in place across the federal government, an October report alleges.The Natural Resources Defense Council report, and comments from current and former officials from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), brings into focus how myriad changes in federal rules or protocol will dramatically increase the public’s exposure to carcinogens. These are taking effect at a time when some forms of early onset cancer are spiking by about 30% per decade. Continue reading...

items.standfirst: Failure to disclose Peter Hindmarsh’s exclusion from practice raises ‘fundamental questions’ over nurse’s caseLucy Letby’s lawyer has said the court of appeal must urgently review her convictions, after it was revealed that a key medical witness in the prosecution’s case was barred from treating patients because of safety concerns.The Guardian revealed this week that Prof Peter Hindmarsh – a crucial expert witness who provided an opinion at Letby’s trial that two babies had been poisoned with insulin – was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023 because his hospital considered him unsafe to treat children in relation to insulin. items.title: Doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby was barred from treating patients during trial
items.standfirst: Exclusive: Jury was never told that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was barred from practising over concerns for patients’ safetyA senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety.Prof Peter Hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that the British nurse had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Jurors were never told. Continue reading...
